filler.paragraph: The condition under study is a recognized health concern for which patients and clinicians continue to seek better options. This study has been designed to add careful evidence to the existing body of knowledge. The rationale draws on published literature and on earlier development work with the investigational product.

Programs and outputs will undergo independent review by a second programmer. Discrepancies found during review will be resolved and documented before the outputs are released. The review process will follow the standard operating procedures of the sponsor.

Statistical programming will be carried out with validated, commercially available or widely accepted statistical software. The software environment will be documented, and programs will be stored under version control. Output will be generated in a reproducible way from the locked data.

The sponsor intends to make the results of the study publicly available regardless of the outcome. Investigators will be given the opportunity to review manuscripts before submission, and authorship will follow accepted scientific standards. Any publication will respect the confidentiality obligations set out in the study agreements.

Any departure from this plan will be documented together with its justification. Changes made after the database is locked will be described in the clinical study report. The version history of this document will record each approved amendment.

Study data will be held in a validated database with controlled access. Data listings will be reviewed for completeness and consistency before the database is locked. After lock, any change to the data will be documented and justified.

The sponsor will arrange for study monitors to visit the sites at regular intervals. The monitors will check that the rights and well-being of participants are protected and that the study is run according to the protocol. Source records will be made available to the monitors and to auditors when requested.

Participant privacy will be protected throughout the study. Records will be identified by a unique code rather than by name, and access to identifiable information will be limited to authorized study personnel and regulatory representatives. Information will be handled in line with applicable data protection requirements.

The study will be conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and with applicable good clinical practice guidelines and local regulations. The protocol and informed consent materials will be reviewed by an independent ethics committee before any participant is enrolled. Each participant will give written informed consent before taking part and may withdraw at any time without penalty.

Any interim review of the study data will be governed by a charter agreed before it begins. Access to unblinded information will be restricted to the people named in that charter. The conduct of such a review is intended to protect the integrity of the study and the safety of participants.
